items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Joe Shuman. I followed them a lot.

ctx.x: It’s a little hard to tell the drummer, look, you don’t need to do that.

No. Because the rhythm — Claude Thornhill had a band too that had a rhythm section that loved the Basie rhythm section. It was Barry Galbraith and Billy Exiner on drums. Barry played guitar. Joe Shuman. I followed them a lot. And Claude played sparingly as well, and they almost matched the Basie rhythm section. And the band played exceptionally soft. They had two extra clarinets in the sax section. They had six reeds. And a great brass section that would swell, and come right down again. Really, it would take…
Wow. That’s being serious about your work.
